tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting an aeration energy optimization program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: aeration is the largest energy use, program must protect nitrification and nutrient targets.

cards.label: Track energy per unit removed monthly and investigate any train that drifts back
Confirm the trial holds effluent quality through a full loading cycle before wider rollout
Review blower condition, control ranges, and dissolved oxygen setpoints against the baseline
Roll the proven settings to the other trains in steps with the same sampling guard
Trial setpoint and control changes on one train with nutrient sampling increased during the trial
Baseline aeration energy per unit of load removed for each train through all seasons

tasks.explanation: Seasonal baselines come before setpoints are questioned, trials are guarded by sampling, and monthly tracking protects both savings and effluent quality.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for completing a biogas utilization study for the main plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: options include boiler heating, cogeneration, and upgrading, gas production varies seasonally.

cards.label: Evaluate the options on lifecycle cost, reliability, greenhouse gas effect, and operational fit
Forecast future gas production from the digestion strategy and growth expectations
Compile two years of gas production, quality, and current use and flaring records
Develop the utilization options at study level with capital, operating, and maintenance needs
Recommend the preferred option and its phasing to leadership for capital plan entry
Carry the gas quality and safety duties of the chosen option into the design scope

tasks.explanation: Production history and forecast come before options are costed, evaluation weighs reliability and fit with cost, and safety duties follow the choice into design.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for establishing energy benchmarking across utility facilities.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: benchmarks will compare energy per volume treated and per mass removed between facilities.

cards.label: Have the outlier facilities explain their position and separate real inefficiency from data artefacts
Publish the first benchmark table with the data quality of each facility stated beside it
Repeat the benchmark annually and track whether the gap between facilities narrows
Collect the first year of data and check it for metering gaps and inconsistent boundaries
Define the benchmark measures and the normalizing data each facility must report the same way
Set improvement targets only for the facilities where the data supports them

tasks.explanation: Common definitions and data checks come before any table is published, outliers are explained before targets are set, and repetition shows whether gaps close.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for building an electricity demand management program for the utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: demand charges are significant, some loads can shift away from utility grid peak periods.

cards.label: Build the peak shaving operating rules with the process limits written in as hard stops
Analyse the billing and interval data to find when each facility sets its demand peak
List the shiftable loads, including sludge processing and discretionary pumping, and their process limits
Review demand performance monthly and tighten the rules as operators gain confidence
Adopt the proven rules into the operating procedures and brief all shifts
Trial the rules through one billing period and compare demand and process results

tasks.explanation: Interval data locates the real peaks before loads are shifted, process limits are hard stops in the rules, and a trial period proves the saving is safe.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing a cogeneration business case for leadership.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: case must cover capital, gas supply, maintenance capability, and the value of heat and power.

cards.label: Size the unit to the gas supply and the site heat demand rather than to peak gas production
Build the capital, maintenance, and overhaul costs with vendor and reference site input
Model the energy value and the simple payback under low, expected, and high gas cases
Present the case with its risks and sensitivities and the decision leadership is asked to make
If approved, carry the performance guarantees and acceptance tests into the procurement documents
Confirm the gas quantity and quality available to the unit across the seasons

tasks.explanation: Gas supply and heat demand size the unit before costs are built, sensitivities are shown honestly, and approval flows into enforceable procurement terms.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for building an energy data and metering program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program will submeter the major processes so energy can be managed by process, not just by bill.

cards.label: Verify the new data against utility bills and portable measurements for the first month
Survey the existing meters, their condition, and the gaps against that requirement
Review the metering plan annually and extend it only where decisions still lack data
Install and commission the priority meters and connect them to the plant data system
List the management decisions the energy data must support and the metering each one requires
Publish the first process energy report and train the process owners to use it

tasks.explanation: Decisions define the metering before hardware is bought, new data is verified against bills, and extension follows proven need rather than habit.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for governing a blower optimization and renewal program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: blower fleet is aging, program links condition, efficiency, and renewal timing.

cards.label: Build the renewal sequence into the capital plan in the ranked order with interim spares cover
Assess each blower condition, efficiency, and remaining life with maintenance and operations together
Trial control and sequencing changes on the existing fleet to capture savings before renewal
Rank the fleet by the energy penalty and failure risk each unit carries
Review fleet energy performance annually and re rank the remaining units on new evidence
Commission each renewed unit against its efficiency guarantee and record the verified saving

tasks.explanation: Condition and penalty ranking come before renewal order is set, existing fleet savings are captured first, and commissioning verifies the promised efficiency.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting a pumping energy program for lift stations and plant pumps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program covers station scheduling, pump condition, and wet well level management.

cards.label: Track station energy per volume quarterly and flag any station that regresses
Baseline each station energy per volume pumped from billing and run hour records
Correct the level settings and scheduling first and remeasure the energy change
Inspect the worst stations for worn pumps, poor level settings, and avoidable starts
Enter the pump work in the maintenance and capital plans with the energy case attached
Plan pump refurbishment or replacement for the stations where settings cannot fix the penalty

tasks.explanation: Baselines and inspection locate the penalty before money is spent, settings are fixed before pumps are replaced, and quarterly tracking catches regression.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for completing a heat recovery feasibility study for plant buildings and processes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sources include effluent, biogas systems, and blower discharge, sinks include buildings and digesters.

cards.label: Develop the surviving concepts at study level with equipment, controls, and maintenance needs
Match the sources and sinks that overlap in time and temperature and screen out the poor matches
Carry the chosen concept into design with heat metering included so savings can be verified
Inventory the heat sources and sinks with temperatures and seasonal availability
Evaluate the concepts on lifecycle cost, reliability, and effect on the source processes
Recommend the preferred concept and its phasing to leadership with the risks stated

tasks.explanation: Sources and sinks are inventoried before concepts are drawn, time and temperature matching screens the list, and metering is designed in for verification.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting utility energy reduction targets and the plan to meet them.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: targets cover the next five years and must not compromise compliance or resilience.

cards.label: Compile the audited saving opportunities and their verified potential across facilities
Baseline the utility energy use and intensity for a representative recent year
Set the target from the opportunity total with a margin for growth and weather variation
Approve the target and plan through leadership and report them in the annual plan
Build the delivery plan that sequences the projects and assigns each saving an owner
Report progress against the target annually using the same baseline method every year

tasks.explanation: The target is built from audited opportunities rather than aspiration, growth margin is included honestly, and a fixed baseline method keeps reporting comparable.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for producing the annual utility energy report.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: report covers use, intensity, cost, projects, and verified savings for all facilities.

cards.label: Have leadership review the draft and agree the corrective actions for missed measures
Calculate the intensity measures and compare them with the baseline and the target path
Compile the year energy use, cost, and production data from the verified metering and bills
Verify the savings claimed for each completed project against its metering or billing evidence
Publish the report and carry the agreed actions into the next year energy program
Draft the report with the explanations for variances written by the responsible process owners

tasks.explanation: Verified data and checked savings come before the report is drafted, owners explain their own variances, and agreed actions flow into the next program.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running a technology screening study for a new treatment need.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: need is defined, several technology families could serve, the utility wants a defensible short list.

cards.label: Survey the candidate technologies and their reference performance at comparable cold climate plants
Present the recommended short list and the screening record to leadership for the pilot decision
Develop the short list concepts at study level with footprint, staffing, and lifecycle cost ranges
Screen the candidates against the criteria and record the evidence for every elimination
Write the need statement and the pass or fail criteria any technology must meet at this site
Score the short list with operations, maintenance, and laboratory staff using the agreed weights

tasks.explanation: Criteria are fixed before candidates are judged, eliminations are evidenced, and scoring by the staff who must run the plant shapes the short list.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for designing a pilot program for a candidate treatment technology.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pilot must answer the performance, cold climate, and operability questions the selection depends on.

cards.label: Run the pilot with plant operators involved daily and log every upset and intervention
Write the pilot questions and the success criteria for each one before any equipment is ordered
Report the pilot findings and the selection recommendation to leadership with the raw data filed
Build the sampling and data plan that covers all seasons the decision depends on, including winter
Size the pilot and set its location, feed source, and operating envelope with the vendor and operations
Analyse the results against the success criteria, including the failures and the operator workload

tasks.explanation: Questions and criteria are set before the pilot runs, winter is included by design, and the report judges results against the criteria set in advance.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for evaluating membrane treatment for a capacity and quality upgrade.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: evaluation covers performance in cold water, fouling, residuals, and whole life cost.

cards.label: Recommend the route to leadership with the pilot evidence and the sensitivity cases attached
Pilot or bench test with the actual wastewater or source conditions through the cold period
Compare the lifecycle cost and risk with the conventional upgrade option on the same basis
Review reference plant performance at similar temperatures and water qualities
Model the residuals, cleaning waste, and membrane replacement duties at full scale
Define the flow, quality, and cold temperature conditions the membrane system must meet

tasks.explanation: Duty conditions come before reference claims are weighed, cold period testing proves the hard case, and comparison uses the same basis for both routes.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for evaluating ultraviolet disinfection for the main plant effluent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: evaluation must fit the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and provincial requirements context.

cards.label: Assess the lamp, cleaning, power, and spare parts duties and the winter operating effects
Recommend the system and carry the validation and monitoring duties into the design scope
Review candidate systems and their validated performance at comparable effluent qualities
Compare the lifecycle cost and risk with the existing disinfection route on the same duty
Set the disinfection duty and the validation approach the selected system must satisfy
Characterize effluent quality, including ultraviolet transmittance and solids, across the seasons

tasks.explanation: Effluent character is measured before systems are judged, validation duties are set early, and the recommendation carries monitoring into design.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for selecting aeration technology for a basin upgrade.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: options include fine bubble systems and different blower and control arrangements.

cards.label: Set the evaluation criteria, including turndown, efficiency, maintenance access, and cold weather operation
Model the energy and maintenance cost of each option over the equipment life
Collect vendor performance data and verify it against reference sites with similar duty
Select the technology and record the performance guarantees required in procurement
Score the options with operations and maintenance staff and test the result for sensitivity
Define the oxygen demand profile by season and hour that the new system must serve

tasks.explanation: The demand profile comes before vendor data is collected, reference sites verify the claims, and selection ends in enforceable guarantees.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for selecting dewatering technology for a plant renewal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: options include screw press, centrifuge, and belt press routes for the plant cake duty.

cards.label: Run trials or reference checks with the actual sludge for the leading options
Select the technology and set the acceptance tests for dryness and capture in the purchase terms
Characterize the sludge feed, including solids, variability, and the cake dryness the outlets require
Model the full cost per tonne, including polymer, power, hauling at the achieved dryness, and maintenance
Set the selection criteria, including capture, polymer use, wash water, and operator attention
Score the options with the solids team and check the ranking against trial evidence

tasks.explanation: Feed character and outlet dryness define the duty before options are trialled, full cost includes hauling at real dryness, and acceptance tests lock the claims.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for planning a supervisory control and data system upgrade study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: study covers control reliability, data quality, alarms, and cybersecurity at utility scale.

cards.label: Assess the cybersecurity and backup requirements the new system must meet
Define the functional needs with operators, including alarms, trends, reports, and remote access rules
Recommend the option and phase the migration facility by facility in the capital plan
Develop the upgrade options and their migration paths that keep the plants running during changeover
Evaluate the options on reliability, support life, security, and lifecycle cost
Inventory the current systems, their age, support status, and the failures they have caused

tasks.explanation: Current failures and operator needs come before options are developed, migration keeps plants running, and phasing follows the recommendation into the plan.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for evaluating chemical feed system technology for nutrient control.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: systems under review serve carbon, alkalinity, and phosphorus chemicals at several facilities.

cards.label: Define the dose ranges, turndown, and accuracy each chemical duty requires by season
Compare the feed technologies on accuracy, reliability, maintenance, and winter operation
Review the storage, containment, and safety requirements for each chemical and site
Test the leading option at one facility through a full demand cycle
Set the spares, calibration, and training standards that support the standard in the program
Standardize the proven technology as the utility pattern and record any site exceptions

tasks.explanation: Duty ranges and safety needs come before technologies are compared, a full cycle test proves the leader, and standards make the pattern supportable.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for evaluating solids treatment technology for a growing plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: growth will exceed current digestion and stabilization capacity within the plan period.

cards.label: Survey the candidate processes and their reference performance at comparable scale and climate
Develop the surviving concepts with capital, operating, and outlet implications at study level
Screen the candidates against capacity, product quality, energy, and site footprint criteria
Evaluate the concepts with operations, maintenance, and the biosolids program team
Forecast the solids production and the quality duties the new capacity must meet
Recommend the concept and phase it so existing capacity is never exceeded before new capacity is ready

tasks.explanation: Forecast and duties come before candidates are screened, evaluation includes the outlet program, and phasing protects capacity through the transition.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running a technology procurement evaluation for a major equipment package.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: evaluation must be fair, documented, and based on whole life value rather than bid price alone.

cards.label: Write the specification and the weighted evaluation criteria before bids are invited
Award on the evaluation record and notify the unsuccessful bidders with the process followed
Score the compliant bids against the criteria with evidence recorded for every score
Brief the evaluation panel on the criteria, scoring method, and conflict of interest duties
Check the leading bid with reference sites and a whole life cost calculation
File the complete evaluation record and carry the winning performance claims into the contract

tasks.explanation: Criteria are fixed before bids arrive, scores are evidenced, and the winning claims become contract duties rather than brochure promises.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for making the full scale implementation decision after a successful pilot.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pilot met its criteria, leadership must decide whether and how to scale the technology.

cards.label: Build the decision paper with the costs, risks, and the option of not proceeding stated honestly
Identify the integration work, outages, and training the full scale step requires
Take the decision through utility governance and record the conditions attached to approval
Confirm the pilot results against the success criteria set before the pilot began
If approved, enter the project in the capital plan with the pilot lessons in the design brief
Scale the pilot performance, cost, and staffing findings to full plant duty with stated assumptions

tasks.explanation: Pilot results are judged against the original criteria before scaling, the no go option stays honest, and approval conditions and lessons follow the project.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for completing a technology risk assessment before adopting a new process.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: assessment covers performance, supply chain, skills, and regulatory acceptance risks.

cards.label: Assess each risk for likelihood and consequence using reference site and pilot evidence
Identify the mitigations, from spares and training to fallback operating modes
Decide which risks the utility can accept, which must be mitigated first, and which stop adoption
List the ways the technology could fail to perform at this site, climate, and scale
Review the assessment after the first year of operation and close or update each risk on evidence
Record the assessment and the decisions in the technology selection file

tasks.explanation: Failure modes are listed before likelihood is judged, stop risks are named honestly, and the first year review tests the assessment against reality.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for developing the ten year capital plan for the utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plan covers renewal, growth, compliance, and improvement projects across all facilities.

cards.label: Refresh the plan annually, promoting, deferring, or removing projects on new evidence
Approve the plan through utility governance and publish the first three years in detail
Compile the project needs from asset condition, capacity, compliance, and strategy studies
Scope each project at study level with cost ranges, timing drivers, and dependencies
Fit the prioritized list to the funding capacity year by year and phase the overflow
Prioritize the projects with the agreed criteria covering risk, compliance, and service

tasks.explanation: Needs and study level scopes come before prioritization, funding fit phases the list honestly, and annual refresh keeps the plan real.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running an asset condition assessment program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program covers process, mechanical, electrical, and civil assets at all facilities.

cards.label: Convert the grades into remaining life estimates and renewal year forecasts
Repeat the cycle on the set frequency and audit a sample of grades for consistency each round
Set the condition grading guide so different assessors grade the same asset the same way
Inspect the assets in criticality order and record condition with photographs and evidence
Build the asset register with age, duty, and criticality for every major asset
Feed the forecasts into the capital plan and the maintenance program together

tasks.explanation: The register and grading guide come before inspections begin, forecasts feed both capital and maintenance, and grade audits keep the cycle trustworthy.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for completing an asset criticality assessment for the main plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: criticality will drive spares, inspection frequency, and renewal priority.

cards.label: List the plant assets and the process function each one supports
Assess the consequence of each asset failure for compliance, safety, environment, and service
Assess the likelihood of failure from age, condition, duty, and failure history
Review the ranking after any major failure or process change and update the duties
Combine consequence and likelihood into the criticality ranking with the method recorded
Set the spares holding, inspection, and monitoring duties that follow from each criticality band

tasks.explanation: Function and consequence come before likelihood is judged, duties follow the ranking, and failures and changes trigger review.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for prioritizing capital projects when funding falls short.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the affordable program is smaller than the need, leadership must choose defensibly.

cards.label: Build the recommended program that fits the envelope with the deferral risks stated for each excluded project
Present the recommendation and the deferral risks to the governing board for decision
Record the board decision and notify the project owners and the affected facility teams
Score the remaining projects on compliance risk, failure risk, service, and cost of deferral
Confirm the funding envelope and the projects that are legally or safety committed
Carry the deferred projects into the next plan cycle with their updated risk position

tasks.explanation: Committed projects and honest scoring come before a program is recommended, deferral risk is stated to the board, and deferred work stays visible.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for completing a lifecycle costing study for a major renewal choice.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: study compares options with different capital, energy, chemical, and maintenance profiles.

cards.label: Present the results with the non cost factors leadership must weigh beside the numbers
Record the chosen option and the costing so future reviews can test the assumptions
Build the operating costs from energy, chemical, staffing, and maintenance evidence
Calculate the lifecycle cost of each option and test it against high and low cost sensitivities
Build the capital and replacement costs for each option from study level estimates
Define the study period, discount approach, and cost categories that all options will share

tasks.explanation: A shared basis is set before costs are built, sensitivities test the ranking, and the record lets future reviews check the assumptions.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for developing a capital funding strategy for the utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sources include rates, reserves, debt, and senior government programs where available.

cards.label: Total the capital plan need by year and separate renewal, growth, and compliance shares
Match sources to project types, keeping debt for long life assets and reserves for renewal smoothing
Review the strategy annually against actual costs, grants received, and reserve balances
Approve the strategy through the governing board and align it with the rate study
Model the rate and reserve path that the matched strategy requires over the plan period
Review the capacity of each funding source and the rules and risks attached to it

tasks.explanation: Need is totalled before sources are matched, matching follows asset life, and annual review keeps rates, reserves, and grants aligned.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for leading a design review for a major treatment upgrade.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior operators and maintainers review the design at the concept and detail stages.

cards.label: Record any accepted operational risks that design could not remove and assign their owners
Hold the review meeting and resolve each comment as accepted, modified, or rejected with reasons
Close the review with a signed record that the plant team accepts the design for construction
Collect the comments in one register, each with the drawing or section it refers to
Confirm the resolved comments are incorporated in the revised design issue
Issue the design package to operations, maintenance, laboratory, and safety reviewers with a review deadline

tasks.explanation: Comments are collected in one register before the meeting resolves them, incorporation is verified, and residual risks are owned rather than forgotten.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for leading commissioning of a major capital project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: new process capacity must be proven before it carries compliance duty.

cards.label: Run wet testing and process start up in stages with effluent sampling increased through start up
Complete construction checks and dry testing and clear the deficiencies that block wet testing
Accept the project formally only when performance, training, and records are all complete
Prove performance against the acceptance criteria over the agreed test period
Train the operating teams on the new systems and hand over the manuals and records
Approve the commissioning plan, including test duties, staffing, and the criteria for accepting each system

tasks.explanation: The plan and criteria come before testing starts, performance is proven over the test period, and acceptance waits for training and records as well as results.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for closing out a capital project and capturing its lessons.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: closeout covers costs, performance, deficiencies, and lessons for the next project.

cards.label: Hold the lessons learned session with the project, operations, and maintenance teams
File the project record, including as built information and the lessons, in the asset system
Close the remaining deficiencies with owners and dates or convert them to maintenance work orders
Confirm the performance results against the project objectives and acceptance criteria
Reconcile the final costs against the approved budget and explain the variances
Report the closeout summary to leadership and apply the lessons to the next project brief

tasks.explanation: Costs and performance are reconciled before lessons are drawn, open items get owners, and lessons are filed where the next project will find them.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for completing a growth capacity planning study for the utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: study links population and industrial growth to plant and collection capacity timing.

cards.label: Identify the year each stage reaches its planning threshold and the lead time its expansion needs
Enter the sequenced projects in the capital plan with the trigger based timing stated
Compile the growth forecasts and the development approvals that drive future flows and loads
Compare the forecasts with the rated and proven capacity of each process stage
Update the study when growth forecasts or development approvals change materially
Sequence the expansion projects so each one starts early enough to be ready before its threshold

tasks.explanation: Forecasts are compared with proven capacity before thresholds are dated, sequencing respects lead time, and material changes reopen the study.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for building an asset renewal forecast for the next twenty years.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: forecast supports reserve planning and the long term rate path.

cards.label: Estimate the remaining life of each asset group using condition and duty evidence
Refresh the forecast with each condition assessment cycle and report the movement to the board
Compile asset ages, conditions, and replacement values from the asset register
Set the reserve contribution path that funds the smoothed program
Build the year by year renewal demand curve from the remaining life estimates
Smooth the demand into a fundable program and identify the years that still spike

tasks.explanation: Register data and remaining life come before the demand curve is built, smoothing precedes the reserve path, and each cycle refreshes the forecast.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running the annual capital governance review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: review covers project delivery, spending, benefits, and plan changes for the year.

cards.label: Compare delivered scope and benefits with what the plan promised for the year
Report the review outcomes and the updated plan position to the governing board
Approve the changes through the capital governance process and update the plan
Investigate the projects with the largest cost, time, or benefit variances
Agree the plan changes, rephasing, and scope corrections the evidence supports
Compile the year project status, spending, and completion record from the project system

tasks.explanation: Delivery evidence comes before variances are investigated, changes are approved through governance, and the board sees the updated position.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for updating the utility emergency management plan.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plan covers effluent, safety, environmental, and service emergencies at all facilities.

cards.label: Confirm the notification duties to the provincial regulator and other authorities for each event type
Update the response procedures, contact lists, and resource lists for each scenario
Set the next review date and the triggers that force an earlier update
Exercise the updated sections with a tabletop drill involving the duty teams
Revise the plan from the drill findings and issue the controlled version to all facilities
Review the incident history and the risk register for the scenarios the plan must cover

tasks.explanation: History and risk define the scenarios before procedures are rewritten, duties are confirmed, and a drill tests the update before it is issued.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for leading the utility response to a major spring flood event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: melt and rain raise flows, flood low areas, and threaten effluent quality at the main plant.

cards.label: Activate the emergency structure, confirm the forecast and river levels, and brief the leadership team
Direct flow management, sampling, and mutual aid requests through the event peak
Notify the provincial regulator contact of the event status as the approval and plan require
Complete the incident report and the lessons review and update the flood procedures from them

Channel B, fed from a clarifier that stayed stable, kept passing bacteria targets on the same lamps and the same days.
A trial week with turbidity restored below 3 NTU brought Channel A bacteria results back into target with no lamp change.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The lamps have aged out and lost output plant wide

High turbidity and low transmittance from the clarifier upsets are shielding bacteria from the ultraviolet dose, and the stable paired channel plus the turbidity trial prove water quality, not lamp output, is the limit
Flow through the channels exceeds the validated rate
The bacteria laboratory is reporting false failures

inference.explanation: Lamp output reads full and one channel kept passing on the same lamps, which contradicts lamp ageing and a laboratory fault. Turbidity, transmittance, and the trial response isolate effluent quality.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Digester temperature log
Return sludge pump run log
Paired channel bacteria results with turbidity and transmittance records

nextClue.explanation: The paired channel record tests the supported explanation directly. The other choices do not isolate dose delivery.

clueText.nc-a: Digester temperature does not test disinfection.
clueText.nc-b: Return pump logs do not test ultraviolet dose delivery.
clueText.nc-c: The paired record shows failures only in the high turbidity channel and recovery when turbidity fell, with lamps unchanged.

Winter flow is too high for the tank volume
Storm damaged baffles have collapsed the effective contact time through short circuiting, and the tracer study plus the temporary baffle trial prove contact time, not dose, is the failure
High turbidity is consuming the chlorine before it can disinfect

options.label: Tracer study results before and after the temporary baffle trial
Grit chamber cleaning log
Influent BOD weekly summary

A new industrial contributor is discharging sulfide to the plant

Split effluent samples analyzed by an accredited contract laboratory agree with the in house laboratory within 4 percent.

Process phosphorus removal deteriorated for the quarter

Primary sludge solids log
Prepared standard check results with the analyzer calibration log

Closed circuit inspection downstream finds a partially collapsed sewer section with heavy debris at the surcharge reach.
A trial after emergency debris removal carried the next storm flow with no surcharging at the same station.
Rainfall during the surcharge events was moderate and below the design storm on the rain gauge record.

The duty pumps have worn and lost capacity
Storms now exceed the design storm every year

Effluent turbidity log
Digester gas log

Interval review shows the plant recovers fully between dips, so there is no long term decline.
A trial schedule change spreading the returns removes the weekday dips in the following month.
Laboratory and instrument checks rule out a measurement pattern.

Instruments drift on a weekly cycle
The weekday pattern is a laboratory artefact

Monthly averaging hid a schedule driven weekly pattern, and the daily data plus the schedule trial prove the governance lesson is to review interval data, not just averages, before judging performance

inference.explanation: The plant recovers fully between dips and instruments check out, which contradicts decline and drift. Dips tracking the return schedule isolate the pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Daily performance review with the return schedule trial record
Grit tonnage record
Effluent chlorine summary

nextClue.explanation: The daily review tests the supported explanation directly. The other choices do not isolate the averaging problem.

Ice thickness on the clarifier surface reaches 0.3 m in alarm weeks, and the rake is observed pushing an ice sheet.
Drive oil analysis and gear inspection in spring show wear within normal limits for the drive age.
A trial with surface ice breaking and a heated drive cover in the coldest week held torque in the normal band at minus 30 C.
Sludge blanket depth and return rates are steady through alarm and non alarm weeks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

Deep sludge blankets are overloading the drive
Ice load on the rake is driving the January torque alarms, and the cold only timing plus the ice breaking trial at even colder temperature prove a winter load, not mechanical wear
Return rates are set too high in winter

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

Torque trend against air temperature with the ice management trial record
Chlorine residual summary

When the measured return load is added to the balance, the yearly balance closes within 5 percent.
Influent and cake solids laboratory results pass quality control throughout the year.

The plant is creating solids beyond normal yield
Cake solids laboratory results are biased high
The unmetered solids return stream was omitted from the balance, and direct measurement of that stream closing the balance proves an accounting gap, not a process or laboratory error

Blower energy report
Return stream measurement record with the corrected yearly balance

Nitrifier bench activity is healthy on samples from both dewatering and non dewatering days.

The plant has outgrown its nitrification capacity
A weekly industrial discharge is poisoning nitrifiers
Basin oxygen capacity is too low on dewatering days

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Centrate load record with the dewatering spreading trial results
Effluent phosphorus log
Grit tonnage record

The sampling procedure document names the flowing tap as the compliance point.

The disputed result came from stagnant side leg water and does not represent the effluent, and the paired sampling plus a clean week from the correct tap prove a sampling point error
The laboratory mishandled the disputed sample
Ultraviolet capacity is marginal and fails intermittently

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Digester gas log
Paired side leg and flowing tap sampling record
Aeration basin foam log

tasks.prompt: A prairie utility sets its nitrogen strategy after total nitrogen removal stalls following connection of a large food processing contributor.

evidence.label: Influent nitrogen rose 45 percent after the connection while biodegradable carbon stayed at its prior value on paired fractionation sampling.
Anoxic zone outlet nitrate rose from 1 mg/L to 6 mg/L, showing carbon running out before nitrate is reduced.
A bench denitrification series restores full nitrate removal when a measured carbon dose is added to the post connection wastewater.
Internal recycle verifies at the design rate and anoxic dissolved oxygen holds at 0.2 mg/L.
Effluent ammonia stays below 1 mg/L, so nitrification is complete.

options.label: Oxygen carryover is suppressing the anoxic zone
Internal recycle has fallen below design
The contributor raised the nitrogen to carbon ratio past what influent carbon can denitrify, and the bench carbon addition restoring full removal proves supplemental carbon is the strategic need
The contributor discharge is toxic to denitrifiers

inference.explanation: Recycle verifies at design and anoxic oxygen is low. Toxicity is contradicted by full bench recovery when carbon alone is added, which isolates carbon supply.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Effluent turbidity log
Blower maintenance record
Bench denitrification series with paired influent nitrogen and carbon fractionation

nextClue.explanation: The bench series tests the supported explanation directly. The other choices do not isolate carbon supply.

clueText.nc-b: Blower records do not test anoxic carbon supply.
clueText.nc-c: The bench series shows removal restored by carbon addition alone on the post connection wastewater.

Influent ammonia load is steady across fade and normal periods.

Dissolved oxygen is chronically too low
A toxic load arrives with the low alkalinity water
Alkalinity exhaustion is limiting nitrification in the soft water, and the bench restoration plus the feed trial prove chemical supply, not inventory or oxygen, is the strategic limit

inference.explanation: Retention, oxygen, and temperature verify adequate. Toxicity is contradicted by full bench nitrification in the same water once alkalinity is added.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

Effluent suspended solids log
Internal recycle flow record

Aerobic phosphorus uptake per gram of solids is unchanged in bench tests.

Influent volatile fatty acids have disappeared
The phosphorus accumulating population has been lost
Anaerobic mixers have failed and the zone is stagnant

inference.explanation: Fatty acid uptake is complete and aerobic uptake is intact, which contradicts carbon loss and population loss. The bench test isolates nitrate competition.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Effluent chlorine log
Anaerobic zone profile sampling with the bench nitrate addition release test
Digester feed log

nextClue.explanation: The profile and bench record tests the supported explanation directly. The other choices do not isolate nitrate competition.

tasks.prompt: A utility choosing a chemical phosphorus strategy finds alum addition lowers effluent phosphorus but results plateau well above the objective.

evidence.label: Jar tests show phosphorus still falling as alum dose rises, but jar pH falls below 6.0 at the higher doses.
Full scale effluent pH falls to 6.1 at the plateau dose, and alkalinity in the treated water is nearly exhausted.
A jar series with alkalinity held steady shows phosphorus continuing to fall at the same higher alum doses.
Influent phosphorus load and flow are steady through the plateau period.
A paired train without alum shows unchanged phosphorus, confirming the alum is active.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

Influent phosphorus has become mostly unreactive
The plateau proves chemical removal cannot reach the objective at any dose

inference.explanation: The paired train confirms alum activity, and phosphorus keeps falling in jars when alkalinity is held. That contradicts weak product, unreactive phosphorus, and a hard chemical limit.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Blower run hour log
Effluent turbidity summary
Jar test series with and without alkalinity control

nextClue.explanation: The jar series tests the supported explanation directly. The other choices do not isolate pH control.

clueText.nc-b: Turbidity does not test phosphorus dose response.
clueText.nc-c: Jars without alkalinity control plateau as pH falls, while jars with alkalinity held reach the objective.

tasks.prompt: Leadership at a Manitoba utility must set a winter nitrification strategy after three winters of borderline ammonia results across its fleet.

evidence.label: A fleet dataset shows every plant that held verified solids retention above the cold water requirement passed winter ammonia, and every plant below it failed.

One failing plant that corrected its wasting to the verified target passed the following winter with no capital change.
Winter basin temperatures were similar across the fleet, between 5 C and 8 C.

Winter temperatures differ enough to explain the pass and fail split

Alkalinity supply explains the fleet pattern

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Fleet winter dataset with direct inventory verification results
Effluent phosphorus summary
Grit tonnage record

nextClue.explanation: The fleet dataset tests the supported explanation directly. The other choices do not isolate retention.
